title: Round-trip base case for the decoder
statement: Fix $n$, and let $f$ be a DNF formula on $n$ variables and $w$ a natural number. Let $\rho_0$, $\sigma$, $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$, and $\rho_0^{\mathrm{dec}}$ be restrictions on $n$ variables (each variable either assigned a Boolean value or left free), and let $d$ be a fuel bound. Suppose that $\sigma$ leaves free every variable that $\rho_0$ leaves free, and that $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ agrees with $\sigma$ on every variable — both those that $\rho_0$ leaves free and those that $\rho_0$ fixes. Then running the Razborov decoding loop on $f$, with width $w$, fuel $d$, working restrictions $\sigma_{\mathrm{dec}}$ and $\rho_0^{\mathrm{dec}}$, and the empty list of emitted advice, yields an output whose first component is exactly $\sigma$.
hypotheses_covered: σ leaves free every variable ρ₀ leaves free
σ_dec agrees with σ on the variables ρ₀ leaves free
σ_dec agrees with σ on the variables ρ₀ fixes
the emitted advice list is empty
caveat: The conclusion is stated in terms of the internal decoding loop `razborovDecode.go`, whose definition is not among the supplied upstream definitions; its precise behavior (what the first output component represents and how fuel/width enter) cannot be verified from the given snippet, so the informalization of that procedure is necessarily approximate.
